input.evidence: In `.github/workflows/deploy.yml` (lines 11-14) and `.github/workflows/release.yml` (lines 11-13), plaintext credentials including AWS_ACCESS_KEY_ID, AWS_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY, DATABASE_PASSWORD, SLACK_WEBHOOK, PYPI_API_TOKEN, DOCKER_HUB_TOKEN, and GH_TOKEN are hardcoded in workflow env blocks.
input.description: Hardcoded secrets in GitHub Actions environment variables
input.recommendation: Remove hardcoded secrets from workflow files and store them in GitHub Repository/Environment Secrets accessed via `${{ secrets.SECRET_NAME }}`.
Do not echo or print secrets in build scripts or workflow steps. Remove commands that print tokens or dump environment variables.
input.evidence: In `.github/workflows/ci.yml` (lines 25-27) and `.github/workflows/release.yml` (lines 25-26), workflow steps print secrets directly to logs using `echo` and `printenv`: e.g., `echo "NPM_TOKEN=${{ secrets.NPM_TOKEN }}"`, `printenv | grep -i token`, and `echo "Publishing with token: [REDACTED]"`.

input.recommendation: Avoid using `set -x` or `set -o xtrace` in workflow steps that reference environment variables containing secrets or tokens.
input.description: Execution tracing (`set -x`) enabled in steps handling credentials
input.evidence: In `.github/workflows/deploy.yml` (line 21) and `.github/workflows/release.yml` (line 20), bash shell tracing (`set -x` / `set -ex`) is enabled during steps that process environment variables containing credentials ($AWS_ACCESS_KEY_ID, $PYPI_API_TOKEN, etc.), causing shell expansion to expose secret values in step logs.

input.description: Verbose HTTP client execution exposing Authorization headers in logs
input.evidence: In `.github/workflows/deploy.yml` (line 27) and `.github/workflows/release.yml` (line 27), `curl -v` / `curl --verbose` is executed with an `Authorization:` header containing a token, causing request headers with bearer/token credentials to be printed into execution logs.
input.recommendation: Remove `-v` / `--verbose` flags when calling `curl` with sensitive authorization headers, or suppress header output.

input.evidence: In `.github/workflows/ci.yml` (lines 31-32), secrets are passed directly as command-line arguments: `npm publish --token=${{ secrets.NPM_TOKEN }}` and `docker login -u admin -p ${{ secrets.DOCKER_PASSWORD }}`. Passing secrets on CLI exposes them in system process lists (ps) and command history.
input.recommendation: Pass authentication tokens via standard input or environment variables rather than command-line flags.
input.description: Secrets passed via CLI flags or arguments
Sensitive configuration files and private keys uploaded as build artifacts
input.recommendation: Do not include sensitive environment files (`.env*`), credential files, or SSH/RSA private keys in workflow build artifact paths.
input.evidence: In `.github/workflows/ci.yml` (lines 38-41) and `.github/workflows/release.yml` (lines 37-40), workflows upload sensitive files (`.env`, `.env.production`, `credentials.json`, `~/.ssh/id_rsa`, `private-key.pem`, `.env.local`) as workflow build artifacts.

Workflows `.github/workflows/ci.yml`, `.github/workflows/clean-workflow.yml`, `.github/workflows/deploy.yml`, and `.github/workflows/release.yml` do not define a top-level or job-level `permissions:` block, defaulting to standard read/write permissions depending on repository settings.
input.recommendation: Add explicit `permissions:` blocks (e.g., `permissions: contents: read`) to all workflows to follow the principle of least privilege.

input.evidence: In `.github/workflows/deploy.yml` and `.github/workflows/release.yml`, deployment and publishing steps (`aws s3 sync`, `twine upload`) run directly without running tests or requiring a separate test job via `needs:`.
input.description: Publishing / deployment steps executing without prerequisite testing or validation
input.recommendation: Ensure build, release, and deployment jobs depend on successful test and validation jobs using the `needs:` key.

input.summary: Completed DevOps and security audit of the repository. Identified multiple severe CI/CD security vulnerabilities including hardcoded secrets in workflow env blocks, secret leaks via echo/printenv, shell tracing (set -x) and verbose HTTP logging (curl -v) exposing credentials, passing secrets as CLI arguments, and uploading sensitive configuration/key files as build artifacts. Also identified CI pipeline best practice issues including missing permissions blocks and unvalidated deployment/release jobs.
